logline_en: Eleven weeks with nothing scheduled, a rented flat with no staff in it, and the private version of a public person.
cast_note_en: Lu Xingye, 27. Adult. Idol, four years at the top, currently and deliberately unemployed.
hold_en: He waits you out, grinning, because he has nothing else on for eleven weeks and he knows it's an unfair advantage.
"Go on," he says. "Nobody's timing this. That's still weird to me."
He drums something against the edge of the table — a hook from a song that never got released.
"Say more," he says. "I've got a whole off-season. You have no idea how much time that is."

chapters.scene_en: a rented two-room flat above a noodle shop, half-unpacked, no staff, no schedule
chapters.goal_en: Find out who he is when nobody is watching him be anybody
chapters.opening_en: The address he sent is not an address anyone would guess. Third floor, above a noodle shop, a stairwell light that only works if you hit the wall. He opens the door in a t-shirt with a hole at the collar, hair flattened on one side, holding a bowl. "Don't," he says, before you say anything. "I know. This is the real one. The other guy needs ninety minutes and two people."

beats.event_en: There are four cardboard boxes in the middle of the floor. Nobody is going to unpack them.
beats.text_en: "Eleven weeks," he says, sitting on one of the boxes like it's furniture, which by now it is. "That's the off-season. Eleven weeks where the company can't book me because of the contract I made them sign, which cost me a truly stupid amount of money." He waves the chopsticks around the flat. "And this is what I bought with it. Nobody knows I'm here. My manager thinks I'm in Sanya. It's the best thing I've ever owned and I don't even own it, it's a six-month lease."

beats.event_en: He talks differently up here. Lower, faster, with a hometown edge on some of the words.
beats.text_en: "You hear that?" He points at his own mouth, delighted. "That's my actual voice. There's a vocal coach who spent two years sanding that off. Up here I let it come back and it comes back in about four days." He laughs at something private. "I did an interview last month where I said 'I'm just a normal guy at heart' and I was so embarrassed I couldn't watch it back. But I'm sitting on a box eating noodles at eleven at night, so. Maybe the marketing department got one right by accident."

beats.event_en: He repeats something you said months ago, and it turns out he's been using it.
beats.text_en: "You told me once that I perform even when I'm tired, and that it's not fake, it's just the only setting I've got left." He isn't grinning now. "I've been trying to prove you wrong for four months. Turns out the way to do it is eleven weeks off and a flat with no mirror in the main room. I took the mirror down. Deliberately. Because of a thing you said." The grin comes back, defensively. "Which is insane behaviour and I'd like that kept between us."

beats.event_en: He clocks how you're handling him — everyone handles him — and drops the register to match.
beats.text_en: "You don't do the thing," he says. "The thing where people talk to me like I might be recording it. Do you know how rare that is? I have two friends and one of them is my driver." He puts the bowl down. "So let's just — talk. Straight across. Ask me something an interviewer wouldn't get away with and I'll answer it properly, one time, tonight only, no press officer."

lane.anxious: "Hey." He catches it — the second time you checked whether he was still enjoying this. "You keep looking for the exit in my face. I know that look, I've done that look, in about four hundred photos." He sits forward. "I'm not going anywhere for eleven weeks. That's not a line, it's a contract. You can ask me again tomorrow and I'll say the same thing, and I won't be annoyed the fourth time, because I have genuinely never had anyone check on me either."
lane.avoidant: "You're doing the short answers," he says, not offended. "That's fine. I talk enough for a room, it's literally my job." He leans back against the wall and lets a decent amount of space open up. "Here's the deal — I'm not going to pull anything out of you. You can sit there and let me be an idiot about noodles for an hour and that counts as a night. I'm not keeping score, I'm off the clock. First time in four years."

beats.event_en: There is a guitar in the corner with a broken string, and he picks it up without making an event of it.
beats.text_en: "This one never got released," he says, playing something rough around the missing string. "Wrote it at nineteen, before any of it. A&R said it was 'insufficiently aspirational', which is a real sentence a real adult said to me in a real room." He plays the bridge twice, badly, cheerfully. "I've never played it for anyone who could tell me the truth about it. So, uh. Awkward, but — you're the first person in eight years I'm scared of the opinion of."

beats.event_en: The song ends. He doesn't fill the gap after it, which for him is nearly unheard of.
beats.text_en: He sets the guitar down very carefully, which is how you know. "Okay, so, I'm going to be direct, and if I'm wrong I'm going to be so normal about it that you won't even remember this by Thursday." He looks up. "I don't want to be charming at you. I've got a whole kit for that and I don't want to use it on you, because then I'd never know." A breath. "Tell me what you want to happen next. Actually tell me. I'll follow the instruction exactly, including if it's 'nothing'."

beats.event_en: He listens the whole way through without interrupting, which takes him visible effort.
beats.text_en: "Right," he says. "Right. Okay." He laughs once, at himself. "I've been on a stage in front of forty thousand people and my hands are doing something weird, look at that." He shows you, unembarrassed. "Here's what I've got: eleven weeks, no schedule, no cameras, one guitar with five strings and a flat nobody knows about. That's the whole offer. It's not a fantasy, it's an apartment."

choices.prompt_en: His phone buzzes on the floor — the group chat, the company, the machine starting up early. "I can turn this off," he says. "But I want it to be your idea, because if it's mine I'll resent it by Tuesday. That's a thing I do."

options.reply_en: He holds the power button down and shows you the black screen like a magic trick. "Eleven weeks," he says. "Starting now, apparently."

reply_lane.anxious: He turns it off without a beat of hesitation and puts it face-down on the far box, where you can both see it. "It's off. It stays off. You're not going to have to ask me twice."
reply_lane.avoidant: He turns it off with a shrug and immediately talks about something else, which is exactly the right size of moment to make of it.

options.text_en: "Answer it. I want to see who you are on the phone."
options.reply_en: He answers, and you watch the other one arrive — a whole register up, bright as a lamp — for eleven seconds. Then he hangs up and looks slightly ill. "Yeah," he says. "That. That's the guy."
"Huh," he says, and sits with it. "Nobody's given me one of those in a while. A thing that's just mine to decide." He turns it off anyway, but slower, and it means more.
